checks.other_parts_regress: Two parts of the plan break things. (1) Adding effective_tokens to improvement.METRICS (scripts/improvement.py:22), or requiring usage fields, rejects every existing run artifact. The tests that catch it: tests/test_improvement.py, whose fixtures carry only tokens, latency_ms and cost_usd (for example test_eligible_decision_never_applies_patch and test_no_benefit_is_inconclusive); evals/skill-value/test_improve_fixtures.py, which iterates imp.METRICS at :81 and expects the positive control to stay eligible; and tests/test_egm_pilot.py::test_valid_synthetic_protocol_export_cross_checks_official_gate, where the frozen score.py emits only the three metrics into the current improvement.compare. It would also open a second efficiency_gain path and a second resource-regression path in compare (:312-318). (2) Editing evals/egm-pilot/pilot_common.py usage() changes the pinned scorer and execution hashes. ScoreEndToEndTests and RunPilotTests then fail with 'contract changed', and test_output_parsing_metrics_and_isolation asserts usage()['tokens'] == 120. Safe form: an optional, spec-declared block (weights by billed model id). When present, compare derives and reports effective tokens from raw per-case usage; when absent, behavior is unchanged. 'tokens' stays a raw integer (integer check at :274). The pilot change goes into the next pilot contract, not v2.

checks.cross_host: Needs a per-host field mapping. Claude's result.modelUsage gives fresh input, cacheRead, cacheCreation and output per model. Claude modelUsage often lists more than one model, so the frozen table must price every id the host uses internally; otherwise runs go invalid after a host upgrade. Absolute values are never compared across hosts.
